Process pathway data for enrichment using 'jam_enricher()'

Source: R/jamenrich-er-methods.R
process_pathwaydata.Rd

Process pathway data for enrichment using 'jam_enricher()'

Usage

process_pathwaydata(
  pathwaydata,
  pathwaydata_params = list(refresh_genes = TRUE, ann_lib = "org.Hs.eg.db",
    handle_multiple = "best_each", empty_rule = "empty", ignore.case = TRUE,
    gene_colnames = c("gene_symbol", "db_gene_symbol", "gene", "ncbi_gene", "SYMBOL"),
    pathway_colnames = c("gs_name", "gs_description", "name", "ID", "Pathway",
    "GO[:]*(BP|MF|CC)", "TERM"), try_list = c("SYMBOL2EG", "ACCNUM2EG", "ENSEMBL2EG",
    "ALIAS2EG"), sep = "/"),
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

pathwaydata

one of the following:

  • Pathways: list of pathways, named by pathway, whose values are individual genes assigned to each pathway.

  • List of Pathway Sources: list named by pathway source, each containing a list of pathways as described above, named by pathway and containing pathway genes. Each Pathway Source will be analyzed one by one, independently.

pathwaydata_params

list to manage 'pathwaydata'.

  • See 'genedata_params' for description of most fields.

  • pathway_colnames: character vector with patterns for preferred pathway column names, the first match with find_colname(pattern, x) is used as the pathway name. For the purpose of this process, only the pathway name is retained, and all other annotations should be retrieved separately as needed.

verbose

logical whether to print verbose output.

...

additional arguments are passed to internal functions.

Value

data.frame with two columns:

  • 'TERM': the pathway name

  • 'GENE': one gene per row, after updating genes when params$refresh_genes=TRUE.

Details

This function recognizes several types of pathway data as input, and returns a consistent format as output: a list of pathway sources, each containing a data.frame with columns 'TERM' and 'GENE'.

Custom parameters

Argument pathwaydata_params controls additional options:

  • refresh_genes=TRUE enables genejam::freshenGenes() which uses Bioconductor annotations to update the current gene annotation to the current version available (to the active R session). Several arguments are passed to this function:

    • ann_lib: the core annotation library, 'org.Hs.eg.db' is default for Human; 'org.Mm.eg.db' is used for Mouse. This annotation database must be available, for example install Rat data with BiocManager::install('org.Rn.eg.db'). Alternatively, ann_lib can be a list with one or more AnnotationDbi or OrgDb objects.

    • handle_multiple='best_each': converts each gene to the best available match, using the priority order defined in try_list.

    • ignore.case=TRUE: Note that Human symbols are UPPERCASE, so for a moderate speed boost use ignore.case=FALSE. Note that Mouse by convention uses mixed case, for example "Apoe", and so for mouse and most other species, use ignore.case=TRUE.

    • empty_rule='empty': converts any unmatched entry to ” or NA so it is not retained in the output. This decision prevents keeping a gene or accession which can never be recognized as an official gene during pathway enrichment analysis. Use empty_rule='original' to retain the original entry whenever the entry cannot be matched to any other annotation in try_list.

    • try_list=c('SYMBOL2EG', 'ACCNUM2EG', 'ENSEMBL2EG', 'ALIAS2EG'): is the recommended order of sources to use when equating a gene symbol or identifier with Bioconductor gene annotations. They are attempted in order, to convert each entry to an ENTREZID ('EG').

      • When using handle_multiple='best_each', each method in try_list is attempted, in order, for each gene entry, and the first successful result is retained as one or more ENTREZID values for each input gene.

      • Specifically, when 'SYMBOL2EG' is successful, it is used. Only when 'SYMBOL2EG' is not successful, 'ACCNUM2EG' is attempted. Only when 'ACCNUM2EG' is also unsuccessful, 'ENSEMBL2EG' is used, and so on.

      • The lowest priority is 'ALIAS2EG' since this association has the lowest confidence for association, and is most prone to multiple associations. In general pathway enrichment is somewhat tolerant to such lower-confidence associations, in return for having more potential opportunities for the correct association.

      • Finally, the matching ENTREZID values are converted to 'SYMBOL' so the "official gene SYMBOL" is associated with the original gene entry.

      • For each pathway, only the unique 'SYMBOL' values are retained.

      • In the event two gene identifiers in a pathway are converted to the same 'SYMBOL', only the unique 'SYMBOL' is associated with the corresponding pathways.

      • In the event one gene identifier is converted to two 'SYMBOL' values of equivalent priority, both 'SYMBOL' values are retained and associated with the corresponding pathways. For this purpose, 'priority' refers to the order in try_list.

  • gene_colnames: vector of columns that could be recognized to contain gene symbols or identifiers.

  • pathway_colnames: vector of columns that may contain pathway names or identifiers. The first matching entry is assumed to contain the pathway identifier associated with each gene set.

Handling other species

In the event the pathwaydata entries were derived from one species, and you want to test enrichment using gene data from species. In this case, the recommended order of operations:

  1. Convert pathwaydata to the most current gene symbols in the species used for that pathway data, for example Human.

  2. Use another resource such as babelgene::orthologs() to convert Human to the corresponding species; or use OrtholoGene to provide a species-to-species mapping to the relevant gene SYMBOL.

The decision to use SYMBOL

The primary reason to use SYMBOL is to focus pathway analyses, and comparison of pathway analyses, on the functional product of gene loci in the cell: a protein product, or active transcript (lncRNA, snRNA, snoRNA, miRNA, tRNA).

There are often multiple genetic copies of a gene locus which produce identical transcript and/or protein products, and the decision to use SYMBOL is motivated to focus on the product and not the genetic source/coordinates of that product.

In Gene Ontology, Biological Process (GOBP), the gene 'RN7SK' (also known as '7S rRNA') is represented only once, although there are over 200 copies of 'RN7SK' in the human genome assembly hg38 as of 2026.

In contrast, the 'Transcription Factor Target' (TFT) resource of the Molescular Signature Database (MSigDB version 2025.1.Hs) contains 'RN7SK' and 97 distinct pseudogenes named 'RN7SKP1' through 'RN7SKP296'. The utility of each pseudogene for the purpose of gene set enrichment is unclear, specifically whether enrichment of one particular genetic copy of 7S rRNA is truly indicative of transcription factor control, or indicative of cell type specificity as represented in the 'Cell Type (C8)' signatures also in MSigDB.

See https://docs.gsea-msigdb.org/#MSigDB/Release_Notes/MSigDB_2025.1.Hs/

The intent of 'MultiEnrichJam' is to use one gene symbol entry to represent any and all copies of genetic locus associated with that gene symbol.

As of November 2026, there are three gene SYMBOL values associated to multiple ENTREZID values in human, which appear to be distinctly different gene products:
